lead.headline: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka sent to jail for five days for entering Jantar Mantar
lead.short: A Delhi magistrate on Wednesday remanded Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka of the Cockroach Janta Party to five days in judicial custody for entering Jantar Mantar after police closed it to protest. A third activist, Ajinkya Shinde, was freed on a personal bond. Rahul Gandhi called the arrests "an act of cowardice".

why.text: It is the first time the movement's leaders have been jailed rather than detained and released, and it moves the dispute over the voter-roll revision from the street to the courts.

more: The three climbed a locked gate and crossed barricades to reach the site on Tuesday, a day after Delhi Police struck Jantar Mantar off the list of authorised protest venues. Police have charged them with trespass, breaching a peace bond, defying prohibitory orders and obstructing public servants. They deny the charges. Das and Ranka can apply for bail to a higher court.

The CJP is a pressure group, not a registered party. It wants the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to resign over alleged irregularities in the electoral rolls, which he and the Election Commission deny. Its leaders were held in preventive custody over the weekend before planned demonstrations and freed by a magistrate.

Rahul Gandhi, who has run separate protests against the Commission, wrote on X: "Students. Youth. Journalists. The INDIA bloc. Different banners, one cause." It is his first public backing of the CJP leaders. The group's founder, Abhijeet Dipke, travelling to Delhi after the arrests, challenged the Prime Minister to "declare the Emergency officially", according to PTI.
The remand runs until Monday. The Supreme Court, which sat on a Sunday this month to bar illegal detentions, is the next place the protesters are expected to go.

update.new: Das and Ranka were remanded to five days in judicial custody; Rahul Gandhi backed them.
update.front: Jail, not detention, for the movement's leaders is a new step.

seconds.headline: Pope Leo XIV has lung cancer; surgeons remove part of his right lung and say the operation went well
seconds.byline: CNBC · PBS NEWSHOUR · VATICAN NEWS · 13–14 OCT
seconds.short: Pope Leo XIV, 71, has lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said after surgeons at Rome's Gemelli hospital removed the lower lobe of his right lung on Tuesday. The 90-minute operation had no complications, the bulletin said. He spent a calm night and is expected to stay in hospital for about a week.

why.text: The first American pope is 71, and his recovery now shapes the Church's plans, starting with a November trip to South America.

more: Leo announced on Sunday that doctors had found a small nodule on his lung during routine checks and that he would have it removed early in the week. Tissue tests during the operation confirmed what the pre-operative scans had suggested: adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.

Surgeons used a video-assisted technique, which goes in through small incisions. The bulletin was signed by the lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and the Pope's personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone. It did not give the stage of the cancer, say whether it had spread, or describe any further treatment. More tests on the removed tissue will be done in the coming days.

Before the operation, oncologists told reporters the outlook would be excellent even if the nodule proved cancerous, because it was being taken out early. That was said before the diagnosis was known.
Leo is due to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November. On Sunday he said he still planned to go; the Vatican has not changed the programme.

facts.surgery: lower lobe of right lung removed, 13 Oct

seconds.headline: Thirteen dead, most of them children, as a boat capsizes in the Ganga in Bihar's Vaishali
seconds.short: At least 13 people died when a small boat overturned in the Ganga near Raghopur in Bihar's Vaishali district at about 8.30pm on Tuesday. Most of the passengers were children and young men going to a feast in a nearby hamlet. Seven were rescued; three or four are still missing.

why.text: Small country boats on the Ganga carry villagers across every day with no life jackets and no limit on numbers, and accidents like this recur.

more: The boat was crossing to Bhagatan Tola, where the passengers had been invited to a feast at a neighbour's house, when it went over in the middle of the river in Rampur Shyamchand panchayat. Villagers on the bank reached it first and pulled several people out; the rescued were taken to the primary health centre at Raghopur Fatehpur.

Police named nine of the dead, all from Rampur Shyamchand. The youngest named was Ankita Kumari, six; others included Naman Kumar, 10, and Pinky Kumari, 13. "Thirteen people have died and their bodies have been fished out. Three to four are still missing," said the Vaishali police chief, Shubhank Mishra. A State Disaster Response Force team and local divers are searching the river.
Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary called the deaths of the children "extremely saddening and heartbreaking" and announced ₹4 lakh for the family of each person who died.
The district has not said how many people the boat was carrying or whether it was licensed to ferry passengers. Those are the questions an inquiry would have to answer.

seconds.headline: Houthis set an Aramco building on fire and fire another missile at Riyadh; Trump weighs joining the Saudi strikes
seconds.short: Residents of Riyadh heard new explosions on Wednesday after the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at the capital. On Tuesday a fire broke out in an administrative building at a Saudi Aramco site after an attack, the energy ministry said. No casualties were reported in either strike.

why.text: Attacks on the world's largest oil exporter push up crude, which India buys mostly from the Gulf, and Indian flights to Saudi cities stay suspended until Saturday.

more: Saudi civil defence sounded air raid alerts in Riyadh and in Kharj province, home to the state-owned Military Industries Corporation and Prince Sultan Air Base. King Khalid International Airport in northern Riyadh has been hit several times in the past week, with deadly strikes on Saturday and Sunday. The Houthis have been warning before they attack airports and oil sites, and airlines have been pulling planes out.

The Aramco strike came hours after the Saudi-led coalition bombed an oil site near Sanaa. The fighting began this year when the Houthis blamed Riyadh for a strike on Sanaa's airport and declared their own blockade of the kingdom in reply to the Saudi one.

President Trump has said he is evaluating whether the US should join the Saudi strikes. Saudi Arabia is pressing its allies for more air defence; experts quoted by AP say intercepting every missile and drone over a territory that size is impossible.
IndiGo and Akasa Air have suspended flights to Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam until 17 October.

update.new: An Aramco facility was hit and Riyadh heard new blasts; the US is weighing joining the strikes.
update.front: The Gulf war has reached the Saudi oil industry itself.

seconds.headline: OpenAI engineer charged with hiding a recording device in its executive meeting room
seconds.short: US prosecutors have charged Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national who worked at OpenAI, with hiding a recording device in the company's executive conference room in San Francisco. He was arrested on 9 October and fired. OpenAI says it has no sign he took model weights, source code or customer data.

why.text: AI labs now treat their own staff as a security risk, and Washington is treating the race to build more powerful models as a national security matter.

more: Staff found the device in late September, hidden in toilet paper and plugged into the USB port of a television, according to the complaint. CCTV showed Alfozan near the room, though he was not cleared to attend meetings there. Investigators say he used a productivity tool to track company meetings, and that a chatbot account linked to his spouse held prompts about recording devices. A second device was found in his bag.

OpenAI said it used its own models to work out what the gadget was and where it came from, and that the FBI is investigating. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," the company said.

FBI Director Kash Patel said Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device" to capture talk about OpenAI's "super intelligence technology". The Director of National Intelligence, Jay Clayton, said winning that race was a national security matter.
If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

stories.headline: Jaishankar says the US trade deal is heading to a 'landing point', and Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar next week
stories.short: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Tuesday that India and the US are ironing out their differences on a trade deal and that the talks are "heading towards a landing point". The US State Department said Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar from 17 to 22 October to discuss energy.

why.text: A deal would set the tariffs on Indian goods in the US, and a Jamnagar stop puts Reliance's refinery, and India's purchases of oil, at the centre of the visit.

more: Jaishankar spoke at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, a week after Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the talks had reached a "plateau". "I think we are waiting on a few things. I wouldn't be comfortable spilling the beans in public," he said. Part of the deal, he explained, is how India fares against competing economies, which is unclear because not every country has settled its own terms.

"The US is today determined to re-industrialise and to reset the terms of access to its economy," he said. "That's what the whole tariff debate is about." Earlier this month the US Trade Representative, Jamieson Greer, said the two sides were working to finish a deal but that one was not imminent.

Rubio will go to Samarkand in Uzbekistan first. In India he will meet senior officials to discuss the strategic partnership and energy cooperation, the State Department said. It is his second visit since May, when he attended the Quad foreign ministers' meeting in Delhi.
The talks began in early 2025. India wants lower US tariffs on its goods than its competitors get.

update.new: Jaishankar says talks are near a landing point; Rubio visits 17–22 Oct.

stories.headline: Sensex gives up a 500-point gain on crude and bank selling, while the rupee has its best day in a month
stories.short: The BSE Sensex was down 0.2% at 72,862 and the Nifty 0.4% at 22,628 at 14:00 on Wednesday, after falling about 500 points from the morning's high. Financial stocks and rising crude weighed. The rupee firmed to 95.09 a dollar, its strongest since 14 September, and IT shares rose again.

why.text: The rupee's recovery after the RBI's curbs is already slowing foreign selling, which has been the market's biggest weight this month.

more: Traders took profits after Tuesday's 1.6% rise. Non-bank lenders were the weakest group: Cholamandalam Investment fell nearly 3%, and L&T Finance, Bank of Maharashtra and Bajaj Finserv about 2% each. ICICI Bank and Shriram Finance were the biggest drags on the Nifty. Infosys and Reliance held it up, and the Nifty IT index was up 1.25%.

Foreign investors sold for a 13th straight session on Tuesday, about ₹1,305 crore, though the pace has slowed. "The RBI measures to restrict speculation in the currency market led to 1.5% appreciation in the rupee in the last two trading days. This has helped reduce the FII selling in the market significantly," said V K Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments.
Analysts say the Nifty needs to hold above 22,750 to draw more buying; it has found support near 22,300 twice this month. Power and capital goods shares rose, with Transformers and Rectifiers up 16%.
Crude is the risk to watch: the Houthi strike on an Aramco building pushed oil up again on Wednesday.

update.new: The market slipped from its high; the rupee strengthened to 95.09.

stories.headline: Apple launches HomeView, a $299 screen for the home run by Siri AI, and a new HomePod mini
stories.short: Apple unveiled HomeView in New York on Tuesday: a 7-inch square touchscreen on an aluminium base or a wall, controlled mainly by voice through Siri AI, and on sale in November for $299. It uses a camera and voice to recognise who is speaking. A HomePod mini 2 and a new Apple TV 4K also launched.

why.text: It is Apple's main test of whether its rebuilt Siri can compete with Google and Amazon in the home, where it has held about 6% of the market.

more: HomeView is Apple's second attempt at the home after the HomePod of 2018, which made little impression. It answers each member of a household differently once it recognises them, and Siri, not the touchscreen, is meant to be the main way to use it. Apple is almost a decade behind Amazon and Google in putting a screen in the home.

The HomePod mini 2 runs on Apple's S10 chip and gains Siri AI, which can tell up to six people apart by voice and give them personal messages. It needs an iPhone or iPad with Apple Intelligence, and those Siri features arrive in a later software update, not at launch. It also adds a "Sound Glow" light on its top, pairing of up to four speakers and new colours.

A Bloomberg columnist called HomeView "so boring" and said that was the point: Apple is betting on a simple device while the leading chatbots stay "convoluted, error-prone, jargon-heavy affairs". Apple's improvements to Siri are more than a year late.
Apple has not given Indian prices or dates.

update.new: Apple launched HomeView at $299 and the HomePod mini 2.

stories.headline: Lisandro Martínez blames Manchester United's board after a 2–0 defeat at Atlético Madrid
stories.short: Manchester United lost 2–0 at Atlético Madrid on Tuesday, with goals from Pablo Barrios after 53 seconds and Ademola Lookman, and Leny Yoro sent off. Afterwards defender Lisandro Martínez blamed the club's lack of investment, said he expected more from technical director Jason Wilcox, and said Michael Carrick had not been backed.

why.text: A senior player criticising the hierarchy in public puts Carrick's position, and United's summer recruitment, under fresh scrutiny.

more: "Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas," Martínez said, pointing upwards. "Really poor, really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment." Asked whether the manager had been backed, he said: "I don't think so. He does his best."

United won 12 of 17 games under Carrick last season but made only three major signings in the summer: Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, plus the back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow on a free transfer. They have won twice in all competitions this season and have their worst league start in 40 years.
"You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas?" Martínez added. "I can't say more."

Carrick said he had only half-heard the interview and put it down to "the emotions of the game". He would find out more before deciding "what and if anything is going to be done". He also said he did not understand Yoro's red card.

update.new: United lost 2–0 at Atlético and Martínez criticised the board.
